 NHTSA Tells 720K BMW Owners to Park Outside Due to Fire Risk
 by 
 TTAC News Staff 
 (IC: ) 
 Published:  November 15th, 2026 
 Share 
 As part of a recall of more than 720,000 BMWs, owners are being warned by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to park those cars and SUVs outside due to a potential fire risk from a faulty seal on the vehicle's water pump.
 Enjoy our posts? 
 Add TheTruthAboutCars as a Preferred Source on Google 
 BMW of North America, LLC (BMW) is recalling certain 2012-2016 3 Series, 5 Series, Z4, 2012-2015 X1, 2013-2017 X3, 2015-2016 4 Series Gran Coupe, 2 Series Convertible, 2014-2016 328xi Gran Turismo, 2 Series Coupe, 4 Series Convertible, 3 Series Coupe, 3 Series Sportswagon, 2015-2018 X4, and 2016-2018 X5 xDrive40e vehicles. 
 The recall is due to an improperly sealed electrical connector on the water pump. Over time, the seal may corrode, exposing the electrical connector to water, causing it to short circuit. The short could cause a fire, as a result, owners of these vehicles are being advised to park them outside until they are repaired. 
 On April 24, 2025, an incident was reported from a non-U.S. market involving a BMW 5 Series that experienced a thermal overload at the water  pump’s electrical connector, NHTSA reported . Preliminary information found that this vehicle had previously received the remedy. It was suggested that an improper repair may have been the reason for the incident. There have been 10 field instances in the U.S. since then related to the problem.
 A remedy for the problem is currently under development. BMW says it hasn’t received any reports of accidents or injuries related to the issue. Once the company works up a fix, it will inform owners. 
 Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed in December 2026. Owners may contact BMW customer service at 1-800-525-7417. Vehicle Identification Numbers (VINs) involved in this recall will be searchable on NHTSA.gov beginning December 25, 2026. This recall replaces NHTSA recall number 24V608. Vehicles already repaired under the previous recall will need to have the new remedy completed.
